task.title: Release claimed one-shot schedules
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/797 with explicit caller-owned recovery from durable claims.
acceptance_criteria: Return claimed schedules to pending eligibility with an exact non-blank durable release reason.
Preserve immutable goal and due instant across reopen and repeated claim-release cycles.
Reject missing, pending, cancelled, duplicate, racing, and impossible transitions with typed evidence and no invalid append.
Keep worker health, lease expiry, retry, dispatch, and execution outside recovery.

attempts.summary: Established RED release and recovery-cycle coverage.
attempts.diagnostic: Focused tests failed because the release value, store operation, latest-release projection, and NotClaimed error did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added reopen, due re-entry, reclaim, cancellation-after-release, malformed replay, and racing-release tests.

attempts.diagnostic: A durable claim otherwise remained reserved forever after process failure, but automatic expiry would require absent clock and worker-health authority.
attempts.patch: Added a reason-bearing released event, explicit lifecycle state machine, exact-revision append, and repeatable claim-release replay.

attempts.summary: Fixed stale full-cycle conflict classification and reviewed scale limits.
attempts.diagnostic: Independent review found that a complete intervening claim-release cycle could leak a raw event-log conflict; hosted review also noted eventual replay cost from unbounded recovery history.
attempts.patch: Mapped same-status stale cycles to typed ConcurrentModification evidence, retained append-only history, and deferred snapshots until measured dispatch-scale requirements justify a separate design.

outcome.summary: Callers can explicitly recover claimed intent with durable reason evidence and reclaim it later without hidden lease or retry policy.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-kernel --test schedule_store

lessons: Explicit release evidence is a smaller and more honest recovery boundary than automatic lease expiry without worker-health semantics.
Optimistic conflicts must compare revisions, not only projected status, because a full lifecycle cycle can return to the same state.
Repeated lifecycle cycles need one explicit replay state machine instead of event-count shortcuts.
Preserve append-only audit history until real scale evidence justifies checkpoint complexity.
